design.question: Does a stronger task-specific scaffold change data collection, unsupported ability, and fixed-data future adaptation?
design.teacher_support: One cached strategy per A training task; visible for first 4 student turns

a_training.matching: Common successful task/rollout-seed groups across all three sources; exclude literal Nothing happens labels, then match example counts

b_training.parameterization: Frozen A + fresh B LoRA; paired B weights and sample order; optimizer reset

design.primary_contrast: api minus generic: paired B normalized raw AUC and gain AUC, with initial ability/NLL
secondary: unsupported A ability and A retention
design.gate: If fewer than 8 common successful groups, report collection result and stop adaptation; do not switch analysis population silently
limitations: Conditioning on mutual collection successes changes the estimand
AUC can reflect prior knowledge and ceiling effects, not only plasticity
Three paired seeds and one B family are a pilot
Task-group disjointness does not imply room or pretraining disjointness
Fixed batched BF16 inference may be sensitive to batch composition
